decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elevated approach toward cup, gradually pitching gripper downward while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Move above the cup's right side with open fingers; continue controlled downward wrist pitch, keeping clear of vase.
Align over cup rim from above; hold height while completing downward orientation. Vase remains to the right.
Position open jaws above the cup's right rim, finishing near-vertical approach before slow descent.
Descend slowly with open jaws straddling the right cup wall; target shallow rim pinch rather than contact with balls.
Close on the cup's right rim and settle at fixed pose; retention will be checked with a small lift.
Small vertical test lift with closed gripper; check cup rises with the fingers and balls remain contained.
Cup follows test lift. Raise it above vase height before lateral transfer, keeping cup upright and jaws closed.
Carry the upright retained cup rightward above the vase, adding clearance before positioning its pouring lip over the opening.
Center the upright cup over the broad vase mouth with vertical clearance, preparing a compensated leftward pour.
Begin slow leftward tilt, translating wrist along an arc to keep cup mouth centered over vase; maintain closed rim grasp.
Tilt interrupted by IK guard. Lower the retained cup slightly toward the vase to restore joint margin before retrying smaller rotation increments.
Back off the initial tilt with very small increments, then test a millimeter-scale downward retreat to escape the guarded configuration.
Retry tilt at 0.02-radian increments while lowering the pivot slightly; keep the cup mouth above vase center and preserve joint margin.
Continue gradual leftward tilt around the cup mouth, holding its center above the vase and checking for slip or early ball release.
Increase cup tilt toward pouring angle, compensating wrist translation to keep the mouth above the vase opening.
Tracking changed during tilt; resume from measured pose with smaller rotation, lower slightly and recenter the cup over the vase.
The previous chunk executed nothing. Test a much smaller pure tilt from measured pose to restore continuous tracking.
Wrist pitch appears constrained. Lower the held cup slightly while easing toward the last orientation, seeking joint margin without further aggressive tilt.
Retreat slightly toward the robot and upward to reduce the constrained forward reach; retain the cup above the vase and seek a continuous wrist configuration.
Re-anchor at the measured pose, then ease wrist pitch away from its stop with small positive-x rotations, preserving the closed cup grasp.
Shift the held cup toward the near-right part of the vase mouth and away from the constrained forward reach, without increasing tilt.
Reverse the recent observed motion in small increments to recover a less constrained elbow-up posture before attempting further pouring.
Begin restoring the cup upright over the vase, reversing lateral tilt so a different pouring direction can avoid the wrist stop.
Change to a forward pouring direction with a small positive pitch and backward/downward wrist compensation, watching the constrained wrist closely.
Continue small near-side tilt, drawing the mouth toward the vase center while maintaining a closed grip and checking tracking.
Tilt gradually toward the vase while compensating about the cup mouth; shift the outlet slightly nearer the center before balls begin to roll out.
Bring the cup toward horizontal with the lip centered above the vase; continue a smooth compensated tilt and monitor ball release.
The latest tilt hit an IK branch boundary. Reverse tilt and raise the wrist smoothly to recover joint margin while keeping the cup over the vase.
Recover from the folded reach by moving forward while easing the cup upright; avoid additional tilt into the guarded posture.
Try the opposite lateral tilt using the wrist's freer direction, keeping the mouth above the vase and bringing it back toward the opening center.
Continue opposite-direction wrist roll with a small pitch relief; keep the cup retained and align its mouth above the vase before release.
Roll the cup farther toward pouring orientation while keeping its mouth laterally centered over the vase; use small increments near the joint margin.
Continue the freer lateral pour direction with gentle wrist compensation, keeping the cup mouth over the vase and watching for ball release.
Bring the mouth lower and slightly left toward the vase center while tipping toward horizontal; closed grip throughout.
Tip just beyond horizontal, shifting the mouth slightly left over the vase and maintaining clearance from its rim.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller tilt increments and a slight upward-forward relief to avoid the shoulder boundary.
Tilt farther past horizontal at low speed, keeping the visible mouth above the vase; avoid lowering into the shoulder stop.
Hold the current tipped pose with closed gripper to let any remaining balls fall; pause rotation after the IK branch guard.
Deepen the pour gently along its current direction while adding slight joint-margin relief; the cup remains retained over the vase.
Increase the retained cup's downward angle while compensating its horizontal mouth position over the vase; proceed cautiously near joint limits.
Hold the downward-facing cup steady over the vase to let the visible ball and any remaining contents clear the rim.
Deepen the inversion gently to clear possible retained balls, compensating the mouth's lateral motion to remain above the vase.
Balls remain visible near the cup opening. Continue toward a fuller inversion with small clearance-preserving increments and closed grip.
Pause at the deeper inversion while the newly visible exiting ball falls toward the vase; avoid moving the outlet during release.
Some balls appear outside the vase, so full transfer is unconfirmed. Begin carefully restoring the cup upright along the recent continuous path.
Continue restoring the cup orientation with gentle upward-forward clearance to keep the shoulder away from its guarded limit.
Restore the cup toward its upright grasp orientation along a smooth rotation, moving forward slightly to maintain elbow and wrist margin.
Continue the smooth upright recovery, moving the held cup toward its original side while retaining substantial clearance above the table.
Restore the cup toward upright with smaller rotations as the wrist bends, lowering gradually and moving toward the cup's original right-side placement area.
Pause rotation near the wrist margin and reposition the retained cup forward and lower, clear of the vase, before completing upright recovery.
With wrist margin recovered, gradually straighten the retained cup while moving toward a clear placement area left of the vase.
Continue controlled upright recovery and return toward the cup's original area, holding the rim until the cup can be set on the table.
Lower and straighten the cup over clear table space, with slight forward relief to preserve wrist continuity.
Finish restoring the cup upright, lowering slowly toward the table while keeping the rim grasp closed.
Set the upright cup down near its original grasp height and gradually release the rim; verify it remains standing before withdrawing.
Withdraw the open fingers vertically from the released cup and check that it stays upright on the table.
After the IK interruption, use smaller upward increments with a slight backward retreat to clear the cup while maintaining configuration continuity.
The released cup is upright and visibly empty, but balls remain outside the vase. Retreat the open right arm toward its origin with continuous elbow-up motion.
The retreat was rejected without motion. Retry at substantially smaller translation and rotation increments to respect the joint-continuity guard.
Ease the empty wrist into a less constrained retreat orientation, with small forward corrections to undo the increasingly folded configuration.
Move the open wrist just beyond the cup, gently reducing the folded reach before retreating toward origin.
Withdraw the open gripper upward and rightward, using gentle lateral wrist rotation to reduce elbow folding while clearing the upright cup.
The last chunk moved nothing. Retry the same clearance direction at half increments to satisfy joint continuity.
Reverse the latest small motion to recover the prior less-extended posture; avoid further folding while keeping the fingers open.
Retreat toward the robot at constant wrist height while gently raising the open fingertips by wrist rotation, reducing reach rather than lifting toward extension.
No motion executed in the rejected chunk. Reduce retreat increments to one quarter to respect continuity near the extended elbow.
Make a small inward-and-lower clearance correction rather than increasing the guarded folded retreat; monitor the elbow configuration before proceeding.
Shift the open gripper away from the cup in small increments, remaining on the right side and checking elbow continuity.
Continue the small lateral clearance motion within the right workspace, avoiding abrupt changes near the elbow's sensitive configuration.
The elbow has regained margin. Withdraw the open gripper upward and backward while easing its downward pitch, clear of the tipped cup.
The proposed retreat was rejected without motion. Retry at quarter increments to respect the sensitive elbow continuity limit.
